title: Detuning- and Stark-robust Rydberg gates
authors: Elie Bataille, Gyohei Nomura, Manuel Endres
abstract: Rydberg entangling gates driven by a two-photon transition in alkali atoms suffer from an adverse scaling of light-shift-induced errors. Robustness to such detuning errors is known to be impossible to achieve in the design of conventional Rydberg gate protocols, where only one of the qubit states is coupled to the Rydberg state. Here, we show that in a more general framework, in which both qubit states take part in the gate, full or partial robustness to these errors can be realized. We present two gate constructions, which either cancel the errors outright or convert them into single-qubit errors that can be corrected locally. We map the regimes -- in terms of light-shift strength, intensity inhomogeneity, and Rydberg decay rate -- in which these protocols outperform the widely used time-optimal Rydberg gate, and find that they already include the conditions of state-of-the-art experiments. Finally, we show the existence of a Rydberg `fly-by' entangling gate, an important primitive for an emerging class of neutral-atom quantum computing architectures.
summary: This paper develops novel, robust protocols for Rydberg entangling gates in neutral atoms that overcome the inherent limitations of conventional designs regarding light-shift detuning errors. By modifying the gate dynamics to involve both qubit states, the authors achieve error cancellation or conversion into correctable single-qubit errors. This advances the feasibility of high-fidelity quantum computation using Rydberg excitations.
main_problem: Conventional Rydberg entangling gates suffer from adverse scaling of light-shift-induced detuning errors, and existing protocols cannot achieve robustness against these errors.
main_result: The authors demonstrate new gate constructions that achieve full or partial robustness to detuning and Stark errors by involving both qubit states in the gate dynamics. These protocols can outperform time-optimal gates in specific noise regimes.
method: The work analyzes the gate fidelity under noise using advanced theoretical techniques, including defining robustness criteria by setting second derivatives of fidelity to zero, and comparing error scaling between different protocols.
model_or_system: The system involves neutral alkali atoms used for quantum computing, where entanglement is generated via Rydberg gates driven by two-photon transitions. The analysis uses a block-diagonal Hamiltonian considering couplings between $|0angle, |1angle$, and the Rydberg state $|rangle$.
key_observables: Gate fidelity, residual sensitivity measures ($S_\epsilon, S_\delta$), and the error scaling relative to noise strength ($\sigma_\delta$).
important_parameters: Light-shift strength, intensity inhomogeneity, Rydberg decay rate, and the ratio $\zeta_{ij}$ quantifying intensity-to-detuning error conversion.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Rabi frequency is kept at its maximum value ($\Omega = \Omega_{	ext{max}}$) and treats errors as quasi-static (Gaussian) for some parts of the analysis.
figures_summary: Figures compare gate infidelity across various protocols (time-optimal vs. robust) under static errors, and show the parameter regimes where the new robust protocols outperform existing methods.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitations of conventional gates, then introduces a general framework involving both qubit states. It presents two robust constructions (error cancellation/conversion) and analyzes the performance regimes, concluding with the demonstration of a 'fly-by' gate primitive.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the primary bottleneck in scaling Rydberg quantum computing: error mitigation. By providing theoretically derived, robust gate protocols, it offers concrete pathways for improving gate fidelity in neutral atom quantum simulators and processors.
